description: Click a row or column of a two-way table to choose the given condition, then click an outcome to see the conditional probability calculated from the counts.

learningObjectives: Calculate a conditional probability from a two-way table by identifying the restricted sample space (Apply)
Distinguish P(A | B) from P(B | A) by choosing different conditions in the same table (Analyze)
Compare conditional and unconditional probabilities to judge whether two events are independent (Analyze)

keyQuestions: Which cases are left once the condition is known?
Does knowing the condition change the probability?
commonMisconceptions: The grand total is always the denominator
P(A | B) and P(B | A) are the same number
Events are independent whenever both can happen together
assessmentOpportunities: Student calculates four conditional probabilities from a new table without the MicroSim
Student states in words what the denominator represents
Student decides whether two events are independent and justifies the decision with two probabilities
